mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate relative to its 12-month moving average signals an active monetary easing policy, which reduces the cost of capital and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in demand, which typically leads to lower corporate profits and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In supply contraction regimes (INDPRO < 100), reduced industrial output and potential supply chain bottlenecks lead to lower corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or the Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 3.5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 3.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in residential construction (HOUST) below 1400 thousand units signals a weakening housing market, which typically reduces consumer confidence and spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1400, or the Rank IC is negative over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and employment (PAYEMS) signal a severe economic contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both INDPRO and PAYEMS decline, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
